title: Background daemon auto-update drains active session and leaves daemon incompatible with current Codex client

### Codex doctor report

```json

```

### What issue are you seeing?

An active Codex session suddenly failed with:

```text
Error: turn/steer failed: Server is draining; retry after reconnecting (code -32600)
```

I did not update Codex or change feature settings while the session was running.

Afterwards, attempting to resume the session produced:

```text
Background server has incompatible feature settings
This session requires api_key_model_discovery to be disabled

Restart will use these shared feature settings:
  api_key_model_discovery = false
  auth_elicitation = true
  code_mode_host = true
  mcp_oauth_refresh_coordination = false

These settings persist and can disable functionality for other clients.
Restart may interrupt active or queued work.

1. Run without daemon this time
2. Restart with these settings
3. Cancel
```

Importantly, this is **not specific to the crashed session**. Running plain:

```bash
codex
```

to start a new session now produces the same incompatibility dialog.

### Environment

`codex doctor --all` reports:

```text
Codex Doctor v0.160.1 · macos-aarch64

runtime:
  version: 0.160.1
  install method: brew

Configuration:
  feature flags: 53 enabled · 1 overridden
  overrides: multi_agent_v2

Background Server:
  status: running
  app-server version: 0.161.0
  mode: ephemeral
  settings: ~/.codex/app-server-daemon/settings.json (missing)
  dedicated update-loop pid file:
    ~/.codex/app-server-daemon/daemon-updater.pid
```

The installed CLI is therefore **0.160.1 while the running background app-server is 0.161.0**.

`codex doctor` shows `api_key_model_discovery` is not among the enabled feature flags. I have not configured this feature in `config.toml`.

The only feature override in my configuration is:

```toml
[features.multi_agent_v2]
enabled = true
max_concurrent_threads_per_session = 12
```

### Impact

This leaves Codex in a bad state when other sessions are still active:

- Restarting the shared daemon may interrupt active/queued work.
- Running `--no-daemon` isolates the new/resumed client from the shared daemon.
- Doing nothing means I cannot normally start or resume sessions because every invocation encounters the feature mismatch.

In my case another implementation session was still active when this happened, so simply restarting the shared daemon was potentially disruptive.

### Expected behavior

A background daemon update should not:

1. drain/terminate an active session unexpectedly;
2. replace the daemon with a version/configuration incompatible with the currently installed Codex client;
3. leave subsequent `codex` invocations unable to use the shared daemon;
4. require restarting a daemon hosting other active work to recover.

At minimum, daemon updates should be deferred while clients have active work, and the replacement daemon should remain feature-compatible with the installed client.

### Reproduction / observed sequence

1. Run Codex 0.160.1 installed through Homebrew.
2. Have multiple sessions using the background server.
3. While using one session, it suddenly fails with:
   `Server is draining; retry after reconnecting`.
4. `codex doctor --all` subsequently shows app-server version 0.161.0 while the CLI remains 0.160.1.
5. Run `codex` normally.
6. Observe the `api_key_model_discovery` incompatibility prompt.
7. Attempting to resume the session that was interrupted produces the same incompatibility.

I did not manually update Codex or modify `api_key_model_discovery` during this sequence.
